newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH CPN TO BOOST 97 FUEL IMPORTS TO 2.5 MLN T.
newsitem.headline: POLISH CPN TO BOOST 97 FUEL IMPORTS TO 2.5 MLN T.

text.p: Poland's biggest fuel distributor Centrala Produktow Naftowych SA (CPN) wants to boost its fuel imports this year to 2.5 million tonnes from 900,000 tonnes in 1996, CPN's head of sales said on Tuesday.

"To keep sales this year on last year's levels we will have to import more than 2.5 million tonnes of engine fuel," Stefan Olczyk told a news conference, adding CPN wanted to sell a total of about 5.5 million tonnes of engine fuel in 1997.
He said the increased imports were a result of lower engine fuel sales to CPN from the country's two major refineries in the town of Plock and Gdansk.
"The refineries are reducing sales to CPN to increase deliveries to other distributors. This can be explained by their will to sell their fuel through their own distribution networks," Olczyk said.

He said the two refineries, which together have a total of 230 of their own filling stations against CPN's 1,366, sold 4.05 million tonnes of engine fuel to CPN in 1996 but would sell only 2.8 million tonnes this year.
Total engine fuel imports to Poland last year rose to 2.6 million tonnes against 2.1 million tonnes in 1995, Olczyk said.
